newsitem.title: USA: Gibson sees little Woolworth impact in '97.
newsitem.headline: Gibson sees little Woolworth impact in '97.

text.p: Gibson Greetings Inc, which had $9 million in net sales to Woolworth Corp dime stores in 1996, said Wednesday it did not expect a material adverse effect this year from the closing of the chain.

The greeting card company was evaluating its business in hopes it could replace the sales that will be lost when Woolworth shuts the 400-store division. Gibson has been selling cards to Woolworth for at least 20 years, said Paul Farley, vice president and controller.
Earlier today, Gibson reported 1997 second quarter earnings fell to $5.4 million or $0.32 a share from $5.9 million or $0.36 in the same period a year ago.
Lower earnings reflected a $1.1 million pretax charge from costs of a workforce reduction in Gibson's Card division and an increase of about 700,000 in shares outstanding.

Revenues for the second quarter increased 4.6 percent to $92.7 million due to improved returns and allowances in Gibson's Card division, continued growth at the company's 190 Paper Factory stores, which sell party goods, gift wrap and greeting cards, and higher sales at its international greeting card subsidiary.

"Moreover," Frank O'Connell, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement, "with a healthy cash balance and very little debt, we are financially poised to pursue an acquisition strategy which we anticipate will enhance and complement the company's business.
"At the same time, we continue to pursue the sale of The Paper Factory, which will enable us to focus our energies on implementing our entertainment strategy," he said.
Domestic greeting card net sales were flat, reflecting continued improvement in everyday and seasonal returns and allowances offset by lower shipments.
Gibson Greetings' cards, gift wrap, and party goods are distributed through retailers and its Paper Factory chain.
